title: Creating Bookend Routines
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses the loss of control leaders feel over their own time as reactive demands pile up throughout a busy day, and argues the reliable place to reclaim structure is at the 'bookends', the first and last 30 minutes of the day. The author offers a menu of concrete morning options designed to be completed before checking news or email, and a parallel evening list intended to signal to the body that the day is ending. The piece frames these routines less as productivity hacks and more as psychological anchors.
points: The middle of a busy leader's day is inherently reactive, so the piece argues the reliable place to reclaim structure is at the bookends.
The morning routine is specifically framed as something to complete before checking news or email.
Both routines are framed less as productivity hacks and more as psychological anchors that signal when to engage and when to rest.
The recommendation is explicitly personal, leaders are encouraged to build their own version of the bookends rather than copy a fixed list.
quotes: Losing control over their own tasks and priorities can be both unsettling and frustrating. Good leaders must learn to cope with this reality.
Taking charge of the day is always possible at the bookends, the beginning and ending of the day.
So, consider establishing a routine for the first 30 minutes after rising for the day. Execute this routine before checking news and email and responding to others.
Repeating the same routine every morning tells your brain you’re ready to tackle the day with vigor and with a positive frame of mind.
Creating bookend routines gives leaders the opportunity to maintain complete control over the most important parts of the day.
